chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id ibn Uqda said: Ahmad ibn Yusuf ibn Ya'qub, Abul Hasan al-Ja'fi, narrated to us; he said: Isma'il ibn Mihran narrated to us; he said: al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abi Hamza narrated to us, from his father and Wahb, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

When the Qa'im arises, there will be nothing between him and the Arabs and Quraysh except the sword. He will take from them nothing but the sword. So why do they hasten the appearance of the Qa'im? By Allah, his clothing is not but rough [fabric], his food is not but coarse barley, and he is nothing but the sword, and death is under the shadow of the sword.

key_terms.السَّيْفُ: The sword, symbolizing military power and conflict
key_terms.الْقَائِمُ: The Qa'im (The Riser), a title for the Twelfth Imam in Shia eschatology
key_terms.تَحْتَ ظِلِّ السَّيْفِ: Under the shadow of the sword, symbolizing death in battle
key_terms.قُرَيْشٍ: Quraysh, the prominent tribe of Mecca

ai.seo_question: What is the nature of al-Qa'im's rule and interaction with the Arabs according to this hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Nu'mani’s *Kitab al-Ghayba*, this narration from Abu Abdillah (al-Sadiq) characterizes the Mahdi’s early phase as one of martial readiness against the Quraysh, reflecting the Shia eschatological theme of purifying the community from its dominant tribe. The emphasis on his asceticism—wearing coarse clothing and eating rough barley—serves to counter expectations of royal opulence, aligning his persona with the Prophet’s simplicity while underscoring that his authority is established through decisive action ('the sword') rather than prolonged negotiation.
